summary: DB-023 created public.event_claims in the active chain (20260928010000_event_posts_and_event_claims.sql). Two things the events lane needs, and one correction. FIRST, A CORRECTION TO THE INBOUND HANDOFF'S EVIDENCE. HF-EVENTS-004-EVENT-CLAIMS-TABLE-TO-DATABASE states that the sole archived definition, supabase/migration-archive/pre-reconciliation-local-only-2026-08-20/20260804132000_event_claims_merges.sql, writes its CREATE TABLE, its indexes and both policies against a table named `ln` rather than `event_claims`, and cites `ln_self_read`, `ln_self_insert` and `idx_ln_event` as object names. That claim is FALSE. The string `ln` occurs ZERO times in that 182-line file, `public.ln` / `ln_self_read` / `ln_self_insert` / `idx_ln_event` / `idx_ln_claimant` occur nowhere in the working tree and nowhere in any object git has ever held (`git log --all -S`, and a `--no-ignore --hidden` sweep of the whole tree: the only hits are the two prose sentences in the handoff itself). The real file creates public.event_claims at line 47, idx_event_claims_event and idx_event_claims_claimant at 65-66, `alter table public.event_claims enable row level security` at 91, and the policies event_claims_self_read (104) and event_claims_self_insert (111). The two policy NAMES the handoff cites as evidence are the two real policy names, which is the likeliest origin of the transcription. The archived file is also NOT internally inconsistent: it is a coherent, if incomplete, contract. The CONCLUSION the handoff drew is still correct and DB-023 re-derived it independently -- there is no row-level guarantee on the claim path, and the service-role call sites bypass RLS -- but it rests on a different observation than the one recorded, and the recorded observation should not be repeated. SECOND, THE POLICIES ARE DECORATIVE ON EVERY LIVE PATH, AND THAT IS NOW MEASURED. All three consumers resolve `.from()` through createServiceRoleClient(): app/api/events/[id]/claim/route.ts:82 (INSERT), app/api/events/[id]/tour/route.ts:35 (SELECT, the ownership fallback reading `status = 'approved'`) and app/api/admin/event-claims/route.ts:21,42,52. service_role carries BYPASSRLS, so event_claims_self_read constrains nothing and the `status = 'pending'` clause of event_claims_self_insert -- the clause that would stop a caller self-approving a claim and thereby taking events.artist_id through the tour route -- is decorative too. Measured on the throwaway cluster: with every policy in place, a service_role insert of `status = 'approved'` SUCCEEDS, and the resulting row is readable. What actually denies a caller-side path today is the GRANT: authenticated holds SELECT and nothing else, so its insert and update are 42501 twice over. The two self-policies are created and asserted anyway, because they are the control for the first caller-side reader or writer this table ever gets, and the pairing (grant narrow, policy correct, both asserted) is the durable invariant. THIRD, TWO REAL GAPS. (a) event_claims.event_id REFERENCES public.events(id) -- the LEGACY table, transcribed from the archive. All three live consumers use that same legacy relation, so the contract is coherent, but the consequence is that a canonical events_v2 event can NEVER be claimed, while DB-009's resolver puts events_v2 first. Measured: a claim against an id that is not a legacy events row is refused 23503 by the FK. Whether claims follow the canonical table is a product decision this lane cannot make. (b) app/api/admin/event-claims/route.ts:53 references `admin.id` with no `admin` in scope in the file as it stands, and both handlers are gated on EVENT_PROVIDER_ADMIN_TOOLS, which is in EXTERNAL_PROVIDER_FLAGS and therefore behind isLaunchCapabilityAvailable('external_event_providers') -- `disabled` in lib/config/launch-capabilities.ts:46, so permanently 503 on every environment value. app/api/events/[id]/claim/route.ts:29 is gated the same way, so the claim WRITE path is also permanently 503 today. The only live event_claims path is app/api/events/[id]/tour/route.ts, which has no feature gate at all.

COMPLETION CONDITION MET, ALL FOUR PARTS. (1) BOTH DECISIONS ARE RECORDED, dated 2026-09-28, as EVENTS-005-D1 and EVENTS-005-D2 (full text in the EVENTS-005 record under proposed_decisions_for_orchestrator; the orchestrator appends them to DECISIONS.md). D1: public.event_claims does NOT follow public.events_v2 and NO discriminator migration is owed -- a claim transfers ownership of an event that has none, the rows it is filed against are provider-imported (lib/events/canonical-event-service.ts:125-128 inserts into public.events with artist_id null and names the claims flow), and a canonical event cannot lack an owner (events_v2.created_by is uuid not null, 20250816133000:51), with claim/route.ts:52-54 refusing the same claim independently. The 23503 consequence this handoff measured is therefore CORRECT behaviour, not a defect to migrate away. The discriminator migration the task record anticipated was NOT authored and is NOT being requested; the decision is handed to the database lane as HF-EVENTS-005-CLAIMS-DISCRIMINATOR-ANSWER so it is not asked to guess. D2: the actor that may transition status is a PLATFORM ADMIN via app/api/admin/event-claims/route.ts, plus the one computed auto-verification arm in the claim route, and `service_role` is explicitly NOT the answer; three application-side enforcement rules are recorded and the `authenticated` SELECT-only grant pairing is ratified rather than revisited. (2) THE `ln` CLAIM IS CORRECTED so it is not repeated downstream, and the correction is ATTRIBUTED TO THE LANE THAT MEASURED IT (database, DB-023), not asserted by the events lane. Corrected at the head of HF-EVENTS-004-EVENT-CLAIMS-TABLE-TO-DATABASE's summary -- the field a future reader reads first, which previously carried the false claim as fact -- with the original wording retained under a new `superseded_evidence` array so the correction is auditable rather than silent. A worktree sweep then found TWO further live assertions of the false claim, both corrected: the ORIGIN record docs/engineering/tasks/completed/EVENTS-004.json:135 (append-only annotated; the origin is the likeliest place for a future lane to re-derive a nonexistent object from) and this lane's own docs/engineering/agents/events/STATE.md. Sweep result: all six files mentioning ln_self / idx_ln_ / public.ln now carry a disproof and none carries the claim as fact, and "ln" as a quoted string appears in no file at all. (3) THE `admin.id` REFERENCE IS RESOLVED AS TO ITS CAUSE AND HANDED OFF, not edited, because app/api/admin/** is outside the events lane's grant and outside its charter. MEASURED: a scoped tsc reports exactly one error, TS2304 'Cannot find name admin' at app/api/admin/event-claims/route.ts:53:48, because withPlatformAdmin (lib/auth/api-auth.ts:251-266) invokes its handler as (request, auth) and binds no third argument -- the value the route wants is auth.user.id, the second argument. This is the enforcement point of D2, since reviewed_by is the only column recording who decided a claim, so D2 is not enforceable until it resolves. The trap is recorded: binding a third argument would silently yield undefined and write reviewed_by as null on every transition with no error at any layer. Raised as HF-EVENTS-005-CLAIMS-ADMIN-REVIEW-REF, which also flags that EVENT_EXTERNAL_CLAIMS and EVENT_PROVIDER_ADMIN_TOOLS must be decided TOGETHER. (4) THE CAPABILITY GATES ARE CONFIRMED AS A LAUNCH POSTURE, not a bug: both flags sit behind external_event_providers, which is status 'disabled' with exposure 'none' ('deferred pending provider approval evidence'), so the claim WRITE path and the admin REVIEW path are both permanently 503 and the claim surface is DORMANT. The only live event_claims path is app/api/events/[id]/tour/route.ts, which has no feature gate and READS a status without ever writing one. D2 records this as the honest state rather than leaving it to be discovered. NO MIGRATION WAS AUTHORED, NOTHING UNDER supabase/migrations/** WAS TOUCHED, AND NO DATABASE WAS CONTACTED (CP-051).
